What ExifLab does, and does not do, with your data
Turns off the map and place search, so ExifLab never connects to the internet. Everything else keeps working.
RAW files are never changed. Edits go to an XMP sidecar next to them, named like this.

ExifLab backs up each photo before changing it, so you can restore the original. Older backups are deleted automatically, oldest first when they take more than %1$s. The newest backup of each photo stays for the whole period.
There are no backups right now
This frees %1$s. You will no longer be able to restore the originals of photos you have already edited. Backups of saves in progress are kept.
ExifLab reads and edits your photos on this device. Photos and their metadata are never uploaded anywhere.
There are no ads, no analytics, no crash reporting and no accounts. ExifLab collects nothing about you or how you use it.
Only two features go online, and only while you use them. These are the only servers ExifLab ever contacts, and requests carry a map area or your search text, never your photos or their metadata.
Map tiles from OpenFreeMap, with OpenStreetMap data, when a map is shown
Place search by Photon (Komoot), when you search for a place
Offline mode in Settings turns both off.
ExifLab can only open photos you pick, photos shared to it, and folders you grant access to. You can remove folder access at any time.
Before a photo is changed, the original is copied to ExifLab\'s private storage so you can restore it. Backups are deleted after 30 days, or when you uninstall the app.

Photos and folders are opened through the system photo picker and folder access. Notifications show the progress of batch edits. Internet access is used for maps and place search only, and network status only to tell whether you are online. ExifLab never asks for your location.
